clue.text: Instrument for new parish church by ring-road

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of parish are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone wants a keyboard for a recently built parish church near the ring-road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring-road' looks like one place but splits into ring (O) and road (RD); 'new' rearranges PARISH into HARPSI.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard instrument whose strings are plucked, popular in baroque music.

clue.text: Opening of mine takes in university examination

indicators.note: takes in means one piece swallows the other inside itself

parts.note: an adit is a horizontal entrance passage into a mine

explanation.surface: Someone inspects a mine entrance as part of a university exam.
explanation.definitionFit: An audit is an official inspection, especially of accounts.

indicators.note: round says the scattered letters surround the other piece
strewn means scattered about, so the letters of Papers are rearranged

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Newspapers are scattered around a hospital ward, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strewn' rearranges PAPERS into PERAPS, and 'round' puts H inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words express uncertainty, like maybe.

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters are put the wrong way, so they get rearranged

explanation.surface: Doing something wrong makes me feel sad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' looks like sad, but here it is the colour; 'wrong' rearranges DOING into NDIGO, after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep shade of blue in the rainbow.

clue.text: Longer route to Scotland, going by air

definitions.text: Longer route to Scotland, going by air

parts.words: Longer route to Scotland, going by air
parts.note: the Scottish song Loch Lomond contrasts a high and a low way home; going by air is literally high

explanation.surface: Travel advice: the slow way to Scotland, flying.
explanation.walkthrough: In the song 'The Bonnie Banks o' Loch Lomond', one singer takes the high road and the other the low road, which gets to Scotland first.
explanation.definitionFit: A main road, and in the song the slower of the two ways back to Scotland.

clue.text: Having dug ground like a pig (grub came first)

definitions.text: Having dug ground like a pig

parts.note: to grub is to dig or search in the earth, as does root
to have led a race is to have come first

explanation.surface: A pig digs the soil, after first going for food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grub' looks like food, but here it is the verb to dig.
explanation.definitionFit: Rootle is a British word for a pig rooting, turning up earth with its snout.

parts.note: an ailment that makes someone look queasy and pale, and is off-putting in the sense of nauseating

explanation.surface: A grumble that puts people off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' is an illness, not a grumble; feeling green means feeling sick.
explanation.definitionFit: An old name for chlorosis, an anaemia that gave a pale greenish skin.

definitions.meaning: John ..., Jacobean playwright who worked with Shakespeare
an arrow-maker supplies archers; The Archers is a long-running BBC radio soap

explanation.surface: A playwright writes scripts for the radio soap The Archers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archers is a long-running BBC radio soap opera, but here the archers are bowmen.
explanation.definitionFit: John Fletcher was a Jacobean playwright, and the same word names a maker of arrows.

indicators.note: maker suggests the letters are made into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: The painter Millais is mocked as a minor figure who makes tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tea-maker' looks like a kettle, but 'maker' rearranges PERIPHERAL TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Millais was a founder of the Victorian brotherhood of painters who looked back before Raphael.

clue.text: Paul Revere, for example, attached to Will?

definitions.meaning: Revere made a famous midnight horseback journey in 1775
an addition attached to a legal document such as a testament

explanation.surface: Was Paul Revere connected with someone named Will?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like a man's name but is a testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Revere famously rode on horseback; a clause added to a document is also so called.

parts.note: rev is short for Reverend, and a cleric's white neckband is fastened at the back

explanation.surface: A rev counter fixed at the back of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rev' looks like engine revolutions but is short for Reverend.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman's stiff white collar, done up at the back, marks out a reverend.

parts.note: E stands for east, the oriental direction
a stranger is a newcomer or visitor

explanation.surface: A visitor from the east who offends people.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who estranges others, driving them away.

indicators.note: Some of the words means only a part of the letters is taken

explanation.surface: Someone promises a piece of chocolate roll in a bit.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean at a future time, soon.

definitions.meaning: to rub something in is to emphasise it
a force or pressure acting on a body

explanation.surface: Massage something in firmly.
explanation.definitionFit: To emphasise, and as a noun pressure or strain on a material.

clue.text: Smuggled quantity by day and held for money

parts.note: to run goods is to smuggle them
some means an amount or quantity

explanation.surface: A smuggled shipment was seized and held for payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Released or held for a price paid by captors' demand.

definitions.meaning: the Bounty was a famously tough vessel to serve on, a harsh vessel

explanation.surface: The load carried by HMS Bounty.
explanation.walkthrough: HMS Bounty was the ship of the famous 1789 mutiny against Captain Bligh's harsh rule.
explanation.definitionFit: A privation or burden; read as two words, a harsh vessel like the Bounty.

parts.note: the Abominable Snowman, or yeti, would wear boots suited to his element

explanation.surface: Awful shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abominable' looks like awful but evokes the Abominable Snowman.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket-like frame worn for walking on deep snow.

explanation.surface: A reliable company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like a company but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Faithful and steadfast, and also fixed, never varying.

clue.text: In new jersey, say, fashion has a split inside

indicators.note: inside says one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: ton is an old word for fashion or style
a rent is a tear or split

explanation.surface: A new jumper, fashionable but with a tear in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jersey' looks like a jumper, but New Jersey is a US state; 'has ... inside' puts RENT in TON.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenton is the state capital, a city found in New Jersey.

clue.text: She has a perfectly good headlight

definitions.meaning: a halo, the light around a saintly head

explanation.surface: A woman owns a car headlight in working order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headlight' looks like a car lamp, but means a halo round a holy head.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, and a halo or nimbus surrounding a saint's head in art.

clue.text: Is it difficult to walk such a dog?

definitions.text: Is it difficult to walk such a dog?

parts.words: Is it difficult to walk such a dog?
parts.note: the breed sounds like something that staggers, which would make walks tricky

explanation.surface: A question about whether a certain breed is hard to take out.
explanation.walkthrough: To lurch is to stagger; the dog is a crossbreed used for hunting.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbred hunting dog, usually greyhound with collie or terrier.

definitions.meaning: to raise the pace of output

explanation.surface: Advance to boost output.
explanation.definitionFit: To volunteer by moving forward, and to raise or intensify.

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A horse's head harness makes a person so upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Halter' looks like horse tack, but here it is a hangman's rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A halter is a rope with a running loop, as for hanging.

parts.note: plant means a factory, and a bank is a riverside

explanation.surface: Something growing on a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like greenery but is an industrial plant; 'bank' is a river's edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A mill driven by a water wheel, sited beside a river.

parts.note: let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: Puffins are allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puffin' looks like the bird but is Puffin Island, off Anglesey in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Puffin Island is a small isle off Anglesey.

clue.text: West hopes to repair the candy store

indicators.note: to repair is to fix and rebuild, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Westerners hope to fix up the sweet shop.
explanation.definitionFit: British name for a shop selling confectionery, what Americans call a candy store.

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: a host is an army, as in heavenly host

explanation.surface: A composer quits the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like departed, but it is L.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Holst, English composer of The Planets.

clue.text: Angry before tea is stirred and drink, presumably

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the next

parts.note: in temper means in a rage, angry

indicators.note: stirred like a cup, so the letters of tea are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, then mixed

explanation.surface: Someone gets cross before tea is stirred and a drink served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is stirred' rearranges TEA into ATE; 'before' puts IN TEMPER first.
explanation.definitionFit: Over-indulgence, especially in alcohol, is the mark of someone immoderate.
